title: Economy Cards Ledger & Rollback Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a consolidated recommendation card experience ('Economy Cards') that surfaces automatic batching/caching suggestions with an immutable ledger view and guarded rollback flow. Goals: make recommendations understandable at a glance, provide a deterministic diff preview for config changes, ensure every apply is recorded with metadata for audit, and ship a safe reversal experience (canary/unwind) so platform and customer teams can adopt automation without fear of silent regressions.
background: Optimize currently generates batching and KV-cache recommendations in isolation; customers request clearer context (expected cost delta, latency trade-offs, confidence) and an obvious, auditable trail when those configs are applied via Console. Engineering has prototypes for atomic config commits and a runtime rollback API; UX must translate these into a predictable operator experience and guardrails for production usage.
acceptance_criteria: Economy card UI shows: brief rationale, estimated monthly cost delta (USD), expected p50/p95 latency impact, confidence band, and a single-action preview button
Diff preview modal displays before/after JSON, token-level delta summary, and an inline safety checklist (compatibility, dependent routes, model variants)
Apply flow writes an immutable ledger entry with timestamp, actor, change diff, rollout policy, and optional runbook link
Rollback flow supports immediate revert and a scheduled unwind (time-windowed rollback), and surfaces success/failure with links to runtime logs
All apply/rollback actions are searchable in Console activity with filters by model, route, user, and time range
Automated canary rollout option available with percent-based traffic ramp and automated fallback to previous config on error budget breach
engineering_notes: Runtime must accept an opaque 'apply-transaction-id' and return commit status; ENG work tracked under ENG-19721
Diffs should be normalized (sorted keys, stable formatting) before storage to make ledger comparisons deterministic
We will store only pointers to the full config blob in the audit store (S3/GCS) and index metadata in Postgres for search
Canary rollout uses existing routing layer; require a feature flag gate and metrics hooks to auto-fallback on error budget exceed — see ENG-20033
Privacy: ledger entries must redact customer PII per security policy; security review required before GA
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Show simplified cost delta vs raw token math: simplified figure reduces cognitive load but may hide rare edge cases; we'll provide an expandable 'calculation trace' for power users
Immutable ledger vs editable notes: ledger entries are append-only for auditability; add a separate mutable commentary field for operator notes
Immediate apply vs scheduled apply: immediate improves time-to-value but increases risk; default to a two-step flow: preview -> canary (recommended) -> promote
Surface model-variant swaps in the diff preview rather than auto-routing to preserve deterministic behavior
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): ship read-only economy cards + diff preview to internal teams; collect feedback (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): enable apply ledger and manual rollback for pilot customers; require security review and audit retention policy (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): add canary automated rollout options, searchable activity index, and retention controls; announce in release notes
testing_plan: Unit tests for diff normalization and ledger write/read paths
End-to-end QA on staging with synthetic traffic to validate canary ramp and auto-fallback
Security review and redaction verification against sample configs
Usability testing session with two platform customers to validate clarity of estimates and confidence bands
metrics_and_success: Adoption: percent of Optimize users who click 'Preview' within 14 days of card exposure
Safety: rollback rate after apply < 2% for first 90 days
Value: average monthly cost delta realized vs estimated within 15% error bound
Speed: median time from preview to apply reduced by 30% compared to manual config flows
